Each operation task carries a small italic f marker."}

An analysis is drawn on the same canvas as a study with participants; each step applies a function to data instead of showing a screen. There are four operations, and each names the code that runs it.

## The four operations

| Operation | What it does to your data | Written as |
|---|---|---|
| `Transform` | Applies a function to the data. The general verb; the other three are named cases of it | `transform` |
| `Map` | Applies a function to every item in turn — every participant, every session, every trial | `map` |
| `Filter` | Keeps the items that meet a criterion and drops the rest | `filter` |
| `Reduce` | Combines many items into one value — a mean, a fitted model, a table | `reduce` |

: The four operations; the palette shows Title Case, the file stores lowercase. {#tbl-operations}

Each is an ordinary task carrying a verb, marked with a small italic *f* badge. `Filter` drops items from the **data**; a gateway changes the **path** ([Data](../reference/data.qmd)).

| Template | What it creates | Prefilled argument |
|---|---|---|
| **For each** | a sub-process that repeats over a collection | — |
| **Read data** | a `Transform` that reads a source into a stream of rows | `data_folder: data/` |
| **Write data** | a `Transform` that writes rows to a destination | `output_folder: results/` |
| **Anonymize Data** | a `Map` that scrubs identifying fields before sharing | e-mail and IP removal |
| **Group** | a `Map` that splits a stream by a key | `key: participant` |

: The five templates in the **Functional** flyout. **For each** carries no verb — it is BPMN's own repeat marker. {#tbl-templates}

## Wire the data

A step's inputs and outputs are not listed on the step: they are the arrows you draw. An association into the step is an input, one out of it an output, and its `transformation` is written `slot = selection`. The arrows *are* the inputs and outputs, so the picture cannot fall out of step with what runs.

Pick the data element by how much you want to commit to. `Dataset` is a store the pipeline reads or writes; `Table`, `Timeseries`, and `EventMarker` commit to a concrete structure. A value too small for a box can be a `bpmn:Property` on the process that owns it, bound in the same **Inputs** and **Outputs** rows.

Set a data element's `uri` and the runner saves the bytes there; unset, the value only passes between steps in memory.

## Name the code that runs it

`implementation` is written `<scheme>://<ref>[@<version>]`.

| Reference | What it names | What happens today |
|---|---|---|
| `python://sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline.fit@1.5` | an import path, which may reach into a class | The Python runner imports and calls it; the `@` version is recorded, not enforced |
| `docker://nipreps/fmriprep@23.2.0` | a container image, pinned to a tag | Recorded and validated |
| `https://api.example.org/score` | a service endpoint | Recorded and validated |

: What each reference names, and how far it gets. {#tbl-implementation}

`additionalArguments` is a YAML mapping of the arguments the arrows do not supply; its reserved `args` key holds the positional ones, and a name supplied twice is refused.

The optional `eeg` schema ships two prefilled `Map` templates, **EEGPrep** and **fMRIPrep**, under *Settings &rarr; Extensions*; they record which preprocessing you specified ([Execution](../run/execution.qmd#what-each-program-actually-runs)).

## Say what the columns hold

A dataset drawn as a box says nothing about what is in it. A **schema** states what each column holds, its type, and whether it is required. A `Dataset` or `Table` points its `schema` at a `Schema` element holding a `format` — `csvw`, `linkml`, `jsonschema` — and a `body`.

| In the `body` | Use it when |
|---|---|
| The schema text itself | The schema is short and specific to this study. It travels inside the `.studyflow.yaml`, so whoever opens the file has the data description in hand. |
| A path or a URL | The schema is shared across studies — a lab standard, a consortium's table definition, a published CSVW document. It can change without you noticing. |

: Inline or by reference. {#tbl-inline}

Open the `Schema` element's `body`: the **Edit columns** dialog gives one row per column — name, type (`string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `dateTime`, `duration`, `anyURI`), description, *required*. A radio writes the table as CSVW or LinkML and reads both back, so a schema someone else wrote opens as columns.

```json
{
  "@context": "http://www.w3.org/ns/csvw",
  "url": "trials.csv",
  "tableSchema": {
    "columns": [
      { "name": "participantId", "datatype": "string", "required": true },
      { "name": "trialIndex", "datatype": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
      { "name": "condition", "datatype": "string", "valueUrl": "#congruent|#incongruent" },
      { "name": "rt", "datatype": "number", "minimum": 0 },
      { "name": "correct", "datatype": "boolean" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Where your field has a convention, name it instead: [BIDS](https://bids.neuroimaging.io/), [Psych-DS](https://psych-ds.github.io/), or the Behaverse [Events](https://behaverse.org/data-model/spec/events/index.html) and [Trials](https://behaverse.org/data-model/spec/trials/index.html) models. `Timeseries` and `EventMarker` take a schema the same way.

| Before you ship | |
|:--|:--|
| Every `Dataset` and `Table` that leaves the study has a `schema` | Column names match the names the steps that write them actually use |
| Units and bounds are stated where they matter — a reaction time cannot be negative | A schema travels with the study as a description of the data, not as a gate on it |
